facts.statement: Tangvayosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous found in the Grès supérieurs Formation of Savannakhet Province, Laos.
facts.quote: Tangvayosaurus (meaning "Tang Vay lizard") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian ages) Grès supérieurs Formation of Savannakhet Province, Laos.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial pelvis, several back vertebrae, a tail vertebra, ribs, and a humerus.
facts.quote: It is based on TV4-1 to TV4-36, consisting of a partial pelvis, several back vertebrae and a tail vertebra, ribs, and an upper arm bone (humerus).

facts.statement: The type species Tangvayosaurus hoffeti was described in 1999 by a team led by Ronan Allain, and the species name honors French paleontologist Joshua Hoffet.
facts.quote: The type species, Tangvayosaurus hoffeti, was described by a group of a dozen scientists led by Ronan Allain in 1999 and the species name honours French palaeontologist Joshua Hoffet.

facts.statement: Tangvayosaurus reached a length of approximately 15 meters, a height of 6 meters, and an estimated weight of 15 tonnes.
facts.quote: Tangvayosaurus llegó a medir aproximadamente 15 metros de largo y 6 de alto, con un peso estimado de 15 toneladas.

facts.statement: The spinous processes of the posterior vertebrae are not bifurcated.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas de las vértebras posteriores no están bifurcadas.

facts.statement: The ischium measures less than 90% of the length of the pubis.
facts.quote: El isquion mide menos del 90% de la longitud del pubis.

facts.statement: Researchers suspected the phalanx formula was 2-3-3-2-1, though only nine phalanges have been found.
facts.quote: Se sospechaba que la fórmula de las falanges era 2-3-3-2-1, aunque cabe señalar que solo se han encontrado nueve.

facts.statement: It lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 to 99 million years ago (Aptian to Albian), in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 120 y 99 millones de años, desde el Aptiense al Albiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: D'Emic (2012) found that Tangvayosaurus was the sister taxon of Phuwiangosaurus within the Euhelopodidae.
facts.quote: D'Emic (2012) found that Tangvayosaurus was the sister taxon of Phuwiangosaurus within the Euhelopodidae.

facts.statement: A 2010 review by Suteethorn et al. resolved both Tangvayosaurus and Phuwiangosaurus as more basal titanosauriforms.
facts.quote: Una revisión más reciente de Suteethorn et al. en 2010 resolvió tanto a Tangvayosaurus como a Phuwiangosaurus como titanosauriformes más basales.

facts.statement: The most recent review tentatively retains the genus because it is different from the only other established sauropod from the same time and area, Phuwiangosaurus, but disagrees with adding T. falloti to it.
facts.quote: La revisión más reciente conserva tentativamente al género porque es diferente del único el otro saurópodo establecido en el mismo tiempo y área aproximados, Phuwiangosaurus, pero se opone a agregar a T. falloti.

facts.statement: Allain et al. referred the old species "Titanosaurus" falloti, from the same geological formation consisting of a femur and tail vertebrae, to this genus as T. sp.
facts.quote: Allain et al. también refirió la vieja especie "Titanosaurus" falloti, de la mima formación geológica consistente en un fémur y vértebras de la cola, a este género como T. sp.

facts.statement: The time range for Tangvayosaurus is the Aptian to Albian stages, from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: This basal somphospondylan measured about 15 meters long and is known from the remains of two or three individuals.
rejected.quote: It was a basal somphospondylan, measuring about 15 m long, and is known from the remains of two or three individuals.
